events.title: Francis Scott Key Writes 'The Star-Spangled Banner'
events.description: After witnessing the British bombardment of Fort McHenry in Baltimore Harbor during the War of 1812, Francis Scott Key saw the American flag still flying at dawn on September 14 and wrote the poem 'Defence of Fort M'Henry'. It was later set to music and became the national anthem.
events.significance: The poem became 'The Star-Spangled Banner', adopted as the official national anthem of the United States in 1931, and remains a lasting symbol of American resilience and identity.

events.title: Theodore Roosevelt Becomes President After McKinley's Death
events.description: President William McKinley died from an assassin's bullet fired on September 6 at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York. Vice President Theodore Roosevelt was sworn in as the 26th President, at age 42, the youngest person to hold the office up to that time.
events.significance: Roosevelt's presidency ushered in the Progressive Era, with trust-busting, conservation efforts, and an expanded role for the federal government and an assertive U.S. foreign policy.

events.title: Great Britain Adopts the Gregorian Calendar
events.description: Britain and its colonies switched from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar. September 2, 1752 was followed directly by September 14, skipping eleven days to correct accumulated drift.
events.significance: The change aligned Britain with most of Western Europe, standardized timekeeping and commerce, and produced the famous skipped days, sparking public confusion about 'lost' time.

events.title: Soviet Luna 2 Impacts the Moon
events.description: The Soviet probe Luna 2 crashed onto the lunar surface east of Mare Imbrium, becoming the first human-made object to reach the Moon.
events.significance: Luna 2 was a milestone in the Space Race, demonstrating that precise interplanetary navigation was possible and paving the way for later lunar missions, including Apollo.

events.title: Death of Dante Alighieri
events.description: The Italian poet Dante Alighieri died in Ravenna, probably of malaria, after returning from a diplomatic mission to Venice. He was in exile from his native Florence at the time and had recently completed the Divine Comedy.
events.significance: Dante's Divine Comedy is a cornerstone of world literature and helped establish the Tuscan dialect as the foundation of the standard Italian language.
